outcome: Answer a dataset reference that names nothing in the workspace as not found (G28): a reference written as one name that matches a dataset only through some of its words no longer resolves silently to that dataset or comes back ambiguous among unrelated ones
criteria: A dataset reference written as one name (no whitespace) that is not an id, name, alias or normalized name of a dataset resolves only to a dataset that accounts for each of its words written in Latin letters or digits: a name or alias token, a token close to or partly matching one, a description word or a column name; words in CJK scripts keep today's scoring

When no dataset accounts for every such word, the answer is NOT_FOUND naming the words nothing in the workspace has, with the datasets that matched the other words as the nearest names, and dataset_not_found advice, instead of AMBIGUOUS_REFERENCE among unrelated datasets or a silent resolution to one of them
References with whitespace (descriptions such as yesterday's sales), exact names, aliases, ids, deleted datasets, and a typo close to a name (orderz for orders) resolve as before

Tests on data unrelated to any benchmark cover a shared prefix only, a shared word only, a name that prefixes a dataset's name, a typo, and a description; the test suite passes; README's resolution paragraph states the rule

dispositions.note: tests/test_resolution.py covers a shared prefix only (lib_reservations), a shared word only (branch_closures, orders_west), a prefix of a name, a typo, a file name, a stem and a description; the full suite passes except the same 8 FFmpeg tests that need libx264, absent from this host's FFmpeg; README's resolution rules state the rule

note: DatasetResolver._score now also returns, per dataset, the reference's Latin-script content words that nothing in the dataset accounts for; a trailing file extension is exempt, so orders.csv still resolves to orders (an existing test caught this). For a reference without whitespace, a dataset with such words is near rather than a match; with no match, NOT_FOUND carries absent_words (the words no near dataset has) and the near datasets first among the candidates, and the existing dataset_not_found advice explains; its rewrite still needs a close name at cutoff 0.75, so orders_west is not rewritten to orders. Also found while reproducing: warehouse_placement had resolved silently to a dataset sharing only 'placement'.
